discovery: Quantum control of macroscopic mechanical motion (cavity optomechanics and quantum ground state of mechanical oscillators)

nominees.name: Markus Aspelmeyer
nominees.affiliation: University of Vienna / IQOQI Vienna, Austria

nominees.name: Andrew N. Cleland
nominees.affiliation: Pritzker School of Molecular Engineering, University of Chicago, USA

motivation: For demonstrating that the motion of engineered mechanical objects, containing billions of atoms, obeys quantum mechanics and can be controlled at the quantum level. Cleland and collaborators placed a micromechanical resonator in its quantum ground state and exchanged single phonons with a superconducting qubit (2010). Kippenberg and Aspelmeyer established cavity optomechanics: radiation-pressure cooling to the ground state, strong optomechanical coupling, quantum-limited displacement measurement and, more recently, ground-state cooling of levitated nanoparticles. These experiments extend the macroscopic quantum physics first seen in Josephson circuits to mechanical motion, test quantum mechanics at ever larger masses, and approach measurement at the standard quantum limit. They now provide quantum transducers between microwave and optical photons and sensors relevant to gravitational-wave and dark-matter searches. Clean, decisive experiments that turned measurement science into fundamental physics.
